- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; reduce forecasted peaks by 5–10% in the following 5–7 days.
- Underestimate prices during sustained downward trends; add 2–5% to forecasted lows if sentiment is negative or neutral.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6), model tends to overreact; dampen forecasted gains by 3–8% in the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2), model underreacts; slightly increase forecasted lows to avoid missing bottoming.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show strong upward trend, reduce forecasted peak by 5–10% in next 3–7 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overshoot early in the cycle; cap forecasted price at 10–15% below the 30-day moving average of recent 10–15 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term price movements; use 5-day smoothing for trend alignment.
